design:
Files (nothing committed, no source files touched):
- `/home/strange/Projects/gpui-go-wt/port/docs/port/DESIGN.md` (742 lines)
- `/home/strange/Projects/gpui-go-wt/port/docs/port/PARITY.md` (660 lines, the index)
- `/home/strange/Projects/gpui-go-wt/port/docs/port/parity/` (22 per-area matrices, `_collisions.md`, `styled-methods.tsv`)

Summary:
1. Upstream inventory, from a scanner over `_ref`: 300 `.rs` files, 190,679 LOC, 6,706 public items (3,099 of them macro-generated `Styled` methods), 869 tests, 47 examples.
2. `PARITY.md` holds totals, naming rules N1-N14, file rules F1-F6, the 300-file map, the deviation registry, examples and external ports; item and test rows live in `parity/<area>.md` so parallel stages never edit the same file.
3. Every row has a rule-derived Go symbol and status `todo` (`gpui_tokio` rows are `n/a:D-TOKIO`); all 4,445 row line numbers were checked against source, and every `path:line` in both docs was range-checked.
4. Layout: root `gpui` holds the whole core crate; leaves are `collections`, `gpuiutil`, `refineable`, `sumtree`, `scheduler`, `a11y`, `internal/{taffy,etagere,lyon,jsonschema}`; back ends are `platform/*`, `render` + `render/wgpu`, `text/gotext`, `examples/*`.
5. Boundaries: cgo enters only through `render/wgpu`; platforms use purego; `runtime.LockOSThread` sits in `platform`'s `init`; the root package has a single writing lane.
6. API decisions: generic methods on concrete types, `Element[RL, PP]` behind a typed `drawable`, and self-typed mixins (`Styled[S]`, `Interactive[S]`, `Parent[S]`) for fluent chaining.
7. Drop semantics: explicit `Release`/`Cancel`/`Unsubscribe`, `weak` handles, and `runtime.AddCleanup` as safety net; the leak detector is ported 1:1.
8. Async: tasks are `iter.Pull` coroutines with `task.Await(cx) (T, error)`, on one scheduler for tests and production with seeded PCG.
9. Re-expressed idioms each carry a deviation id (20 in total, D-NAME through D-MACRO); section 5.8 lists what stays 1:1 (effect queue, entity map, window phases, key dispatch, style cascade, scene, text layout, elements, test scheduler, shaders).
10. Codegen is in-repo `go:generate` tools: `stylegen`, `refinegen`, `actiongen`, `wlgen`, plus `paritycheck` for CI.
11. Stage plan S0-S23 across three lanes; S0 bootstraps the repo files and CI, and S3 lands all shared contracts so later stages run in parallel.
12. Milestones follow M0-M4; M1 exit is the `hello_world` window and quads on Hyprland, and its text only appears at M2 exit.
13. The language-level API shapes were compile-checked on go1.27.4 in scratch programs (mixins, generic methods, `iter.Pull` under `LockOSThread`, `weak`, `AddCleanup`, `encoding/json/v2`); nothing of the port itself is built yet.
14. Parity limits are only the three allowed ones (L-GLYPH, L-JPEG, L-SVGTEXT); risks and their containment are in section 12.
15. Open items needing an owner decision (section 14):
    - Wayland must bind libwayland-client via purego, because the Vulkan surface needs `wl_surface*`/`wl_display*`.
    - A D-Bus library is needed and is not in `RESEARCH-deps.md`.
    - The missing WebGL fallback, wgpu-native v29 vs v30, and web threading are not in the allowed limits.
    - The JSON schema reflector and screen capture are unplanned.
decisions: Read first, in this order: your stage's section in docs/port/STAGES.md (the full brief with file list, sizes and tests; the stage record handed to you is only its summary), docs/port/DESIGN.md sections 5, 6 and 9, docs/port/PARITY.md section 3, and docs/api-contracts.md once it exists. They are binding. Where STAGES.md differs from DESIGN or PARITY, STAGES.md wins.

Port, do not redesign: upstream is zed @ 6501df15765d66d6c2a2b66b1eb22434ccef3f86. Keep upstream's names (PARITY rules N1-N14), order of operations, constants and panic messages. Re-express only what DESIGN 5.1-5.7 lists (D-NAME, D-RAII, D-OPT, D-VOID, D-EMIT, D-COND, D-INTO, D-GEOM, D-STRING, D-ASYNC, D-RNG, D-ARENA, D-TOKIO, D-HOTRELOAD, D-PROPTEST, D-BENCH, D-SCHEMA, D-FEATURE, D-HTTP, D-MACRO).

Reference sources are read-only: `_ref/<crate>/` for Zed; Rust dependencies under `~/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/<crate>-<version>/` (taffy-0.15.0, etagere-0.2.15, lyon_path-1.0.19, lyon_geom-1.0.20, tiny-skia-path-0.11.4, accesskit-0.24.1, accesskit_consumer-0.38.0, accesskit_atspi_common-0.19.1, accesskit_unix-0.22.1, accesskit_macos-0.26.3, accesskit_windows-0.34.0, cosmic-text-0.19.0, zed-xim-0.4.0-zed, xim-parser-0.2.2, xim-ctext-0.3.0, x11-clipboard-0.9.3, x11rb-protocol-0.13.2, xkbcommon-0.8.0, wayland-protocols-wlr-0.3.12, wayland-protocols-plasma-0.3.12); taffy's test suite in `_ext/taffy` (gitignored clone of tag v0.15.0); Wayland XML in /usr/share/wayland and /usr/share/wayland-protocols.

Layout: module `github.com/megascan/gpui-go`, Go 1.27; root package `gpui`; packages collections, gpuiutil, refineable, sumtree, scheduler, a11y (+ a11y/consumer, a11y/atspi, a11y/macos, a11y/windows), internal/taffy, internal/etagere, internal/lyon, internal/jsonschema, internal/cmd/{paritycheck,refinegen,actiongen,stylegen,wlgen,wlspike,shoot}, render, render/wgpu, text/gotext, platform, platform/linux (+ internal/common, internal/wl, internal/wlproto, internal/xkb, internal/xcbshim, wayland, x11), platform/apple, platform/macos, platform/ios, platform/windows, platform/web, examples/<name>. One upstream file maps to one Go file (PARITY F1-F6).

The root package has one writer at a time: root stages form a chain through dependsOn. Forward references live in root `stubs.go`: a stage that ports a file deletes that file's symbols from stubs.go and may add panicking stubs (panic with `gpui: unimplemented <symbol>`) with final signatures for symbols a later stage owns. Other packages only compile against stubs and never call them in tests. stubs.go is deleted by M3-root-misc. internal/taffy and the two Linux backend packages use the same pattern with a package-local stubs.go.

A piece never shares a Go package with its stage's core task or with another piece, so pieces can be built at the same time without breaking each other's build. Stay inside your owned paths. A bug in a package you do not own: write a minimal failing repro in your own paths and an entry in docs/port/handoff/<stage>.md; exit stages (M0-exit, M1-exit, M2-exit, M3-exit, M4-ci-macos, M4-ci-windows, M4-exit) have fix authority and work through those files.

File rule exceptions: window.rs is split into window.go (lines 1-2561, 7891-8411), window_paint.go (2562-5700), window_dispatch.go (5700-7890), window_test.go; div.rs into elements_div.go (1-1904 + Interactivity struct), elements_div_paint.go (1905-4539), elements_div_test.go. Documentation goes under lowercase `docs/` (port tracking in docs/port/); never create `DOCS/`, the macOS and Windows runners have case-insensitive file systems. PARITY F6's `DOCS/` pages become docs/*.md.

go.mod and go.sum are owned by M0-bootstrap and already require every module in the installs list. Builders never run `go get`, `go mod tidy` or `go install` and never add a dependency; if one is missing, stop and write it to docs/port/handoff/<stage>.md. Pinned: purego v0.11.3, oliverbestmann/webgpu v1.38.1, go-text/typesetting v0.3.5, xo/okage v0.20.1, jezek/xgb v1.3.1, jezek/xgbutil v0.0.0-20260124183602-9fd151d6a51a, godbus/dbus/v5 v5.2.4, x/image v0.48.0, x/sys v0.50.0, gen2brain/avif v0.6.0.

Parity bookkeeping: each stage edits only the area files in its owns list, row by row (never rewrite a whole file), in the same change as the code. Status is `todo`, `done`, `dev:<id>`, `n/a:<id>` or `blocked:<stage name|owner>` (a test or item that needs a later stage or an owner decision). New deviation ids are registered in a `## Deviations registered here` table at the end of the stage's own area file, not in PARITY.md. Items the scan missed get new rows. `go run ./internal/cmd/paritycheck -area <a> [-done <upstream prefix>,...] [-all-done [-allow-owner]] [-lint] [-rescan]` must pass before a stage is finished. External ports get docs/port/parity/ext-<name>.md created by their first stage.

AGENT.md, TECH_DEBT.md, docs/port/PARITY.md and .github/workflows/ci.yml are edited only by M0-bootstrap and the exit stages. Every other stage writes hacks and known issues to docs/port/debt/<stage>.md at the moment it writes them, handoffs to docs/port/handoff/<stage>.md, and on completion creates docs/port/status/<stage>.done with its verify result (one file per stage, so there are no edit conflicts).

Go API shape (DESIGN 5-6): generic methods on concrete types (`Entity[T].Update`, `App.New`, `Context[T].Subscribe`), free generic functions only where the receiver would be an interface; closures returning a value use the `R` suffix (`Update` / `UpdateR`); `anyhow::Result<T>` -> `(T, error)`, panics stay panics; returned `Option<T>` -> `(T, bool)` or a nil-able type, Option struct fields -> `gpui.Option[T]` (alias of gpuiutil.Option); iterators -> iter.Seq / iter.Seq2, `impl IntoIterator` parameters -> slices or variadics; field-less enums -> `type X uint8` with `XVariant` constants, data enums -> sealed interfaces or comparable tagged structs; `impl Into<X>` -> the concrete type, a sealed `IntoX` interface, or a union-constrained generic; TypeId -> reflect.Type; `gpui.Task[T]` is an alias of scheduler.Task[T].

Elements: `Element[RL, PP]` with typed state behind an unexported drawable, never `any`. Fluent traits are self-typed mixins embedded in each element (`Styled[S]`, `Interactive[S]`, `StatefulInteractive[S]`, `Parent[S]`, `Fluent[S]`) and bound in the element's constructor with the helpers documented in docs/api-contracts.md; chains keep the concrete type (`NewDiv().Flex().SizeFull()` is `*Div`). No element type may declare a method whose name is in docs/port/parity/styled-methods.tsv or the interactive method sets. `Element::id` is `ElementID`; constructors that collide with a type are `New<Type>`.

Handles (D-RAII): a handle value aliases one counted handle; `Clone()` makes a new one, `Release()` is the explicit drop (idempotent, use after release panics). Ported code calls Release / Cancel / Unsubscribe / Detach exactly where upstream drops, calls `detach()`, or lets a value go out of scope. Subscriptions and tasks never stop because of garbage collection; runtime.AddCleanup is only the safety net for entity and focus handles and the leak reporter. Tests in this repo run with strict leak detection.

Async (D-ASYNC): tasks are iter.Pull coroutines scheduled by the scheduler package in tests and production; `.await` is `task.Await(cx)`; a foreground task holds `*AsyncApp`, not `*App`, and blocks only in gpui / scheduler primitives (Await, Timer, Chan, Oneshot, Select, Yield), never on a raw channel, mutex wait or time.Sleep. Test randomness comes from the scheduler's seeded PCG (D-RNG).

Actions: an action type implements `Name`, `BoxedClone`, `PartialEq` and registers itself with `gpui.RegisterAction` from `init` (by hand or with the `//gpui:action` directive and actiongen). JSON goes through encoding/json/v2 and encoding/json/jsontext everywhere in the port; schemas through internal/jsonschema.

Tests: every upstream test is one Go test named by rule N14 (`TestKeymap_Foo`, inner module name after the file stem), in `<file>_test.go` of the same package; `#[gpui::test]` bodies run inside `gpui.RunTest` with upstream's seeds / iterations / retries; `#[ignore]` becomes t.Skip with upstream's reason; cfg(target_os) gates become build constraints; benches become `Benchmark<File>_<Name>` on gpui.RunBench. Fix the code, not the test, when a ported test fails. Test support (TestAppContext, TestPlatform) lives in ordinary files of the root package.

Test isolation on the developer's machine: `go test` never opens a window, never talks to the session bus, the a11y bus, the keyring, the notification daemon or the system clipboard, and never starts or stops user services. Tests that need a display run only with GPUI_TEST_DISPLAY=1; D-Bus tests use a fake connection or a private dbus-daemon started by the test; credential tests use unique names and delete only what they created; GPU tests skip when no adapter is found.

Generated code is committed, named `*_gen.go`, starts with `// Code generated by <tool>; DO NOT EDIT.`, and is produced by a `//go:generate go run github.com/megascan/gpui-go/internal/cmd/<tool> ...` line in a hand-written file of the same package; `go generate ./...` must leave every generated file byte-identical (verify with checksums, not `git diff`: the tree is not committed between stages). Directives are `//gpui:refineable` and `//gpui:action`.

Build rules: the root package imports no platform, renderer, cgo or purego code (DESIGN section 4 import rules, enforced by `paritycheck -lint`); render/wgpu is the only package with cgo and is constrained to `linux || js`; Linux packages are `linux`, Apple packages `darwin` (macos: `darwin && !ios`, ios: `ios`), platform/windows `windows`, platform/web `js && wasm`. Everything except render/wgpu must pass `CGO_ENABLED=0 go vet` for darwin, windows and js/wasm from Linux. `runtime.LockOSThread()` is called in `init` of package platform only; the root package never locks a thread. File stems never end in a GOOS / GOARCH word by accident (F3).

Seams between packages: platform windows hold a `render.Renderer` (interface in package render); Linux constructs it with `wgpu.NewRenderer`, macOS and Windows with their own renderers; all atlases use internal/etagere. The Linux and web text system is text/gotext (`NewTextSystem`, `NewTextSystemWithoutSystemFonts`). Conversions between gpui types and internal/taffy, internal/etagere or internal/lyon types live in the bridge files (taffy.go, path_builder.go, the atlas implementations), never in geometry.go, style.go or platform.go. Each platform window package has an `a11y.go` seam that the adapter stages fill.

GPU data: scene primitive structs keep upstream field order with fixed-size 4-byte-aligned fields and are uploaded with unsafe.Slice; scene_layout_test.go pins sizes and offsets. Shader files (4 WGSL, shaders.metal, shaders.hlsl, alpha_correction.hlsl) are byte-identical copies embedded with //go:embed and checked by sha256 against `_ref`.

Code style: gofmt; no comments in code except terse godoc on exported API (first sentence starts with the symbol name), `//go:` and `//gpui:` directives and generated-file headers; no per-file licence headers (LICENSE + NOTICE cover it); errors wrapped with `%w`; no new third-party dependency; no `init` side effects other than registration and the platform thread lock.

Verification: a stage is finished when `sh /home/strange/Projects/gpui-go-wt/port/docs/port/verify.sh <stage>` exits 0. It runs exactly the commands in the stage's Verify block in STAGES.md (build, vet, test and gofmt on the stage's own packages, plus paritycheck), never a whole-repo build except in exit stages. Builders do not edit verify.sh or STAGES.md; an exit stage may, changing both together.

Running things: shell commands start with `cd /home/strange/Projects/gpui-go-wt/port &&` (the working directory resets between calls). Anything that can take more than about 20 seconds (full test runs, cgo builds of render/wgpu, CI waits) runs in the background; never sleep-poll in the foreground. Run examples and spikes only through internal/cmd/shoot or with `timeout`, at low priority, and leave no window, process or headless output behind.

Screenshots: internal/cmd/shoot (built in M1-exit) is the only way examples are captured; images go to docs/port/screenshots/<group>/<example>.png. Open every image with the Read tool and check it for missing content, clipping, blur and wrong framing before it is recorded as verified. What cannot be checked on this machine (macOS, Windows, iOS, a browser) is written to docs/port/OWNER-CHECKS.md as `YOU: <what to check, where>`; it is never claimed as verified.

Git: branch feat/port, base dev, no Co-Authored-By lines. Only the exit and CI stages commit and push, and only the paths of stages that have a docs/port/status/<stage>.done file (skip if the harness already committed them); never `git add -A`, never force-push. M0-exit opens the draft PR so the macOS and Windows runners compile the root and leaf packages from then on. The M4 platform packages (platform/apple, macos, ios, windows, web, a11y/macos, a11y/windows) are first committed by M4-ci-macos, M4-ci-windows and M4-exit, so an unfinished platform never turns an earlier exit stage's CI red.

Scheduling: at most three stages run at once; when more are ready, take the earliest in the order of docs/port/STAGES.md (milestone order). The root chain is the critical path; the other two lanes feed it first (foundation, scheduler, a11y schema, jsonschema, lyon, taffy, sumtree).

Assumed answers to DESIGN section 14, to be confirmed by the owner: (1) Wayland goes through libwayland-client with purego, with bindings from the in-repo generator; (2) D-Bus is github.com/godbus/dbus/v5; (3) accessibility adapters are native Go ports of accesskit_consumer / atspi / macos / windows, not accesskit-c; (4) action JSON schema comes from internal/jsonschema; (5) what the chosen libraries cannot do (WebGL fallback, multi-threaded web dispatcher, wgpu-native v29 vs upstream v30 differences, screen-capture back ends, iOS gaps) is ported up to the interface and its rows are `blocked:owner`; they are reported, never silently turned into limits.

Known parity limits are only L-GLYPH (Linux glyph pixels vs swash), L-JPEG (JPEG decode values) and L-SVGTEXT (text and embedded images inside SVG); each row using one cites the id. Licence: Apache-2.0 LICENSE plus NOTICE crediting Zed Industries (GPUI is Apache-2.0).

stages.name: M0-bootstrap
stages.goal: Create the module, licence files, agent docs, CI workflow, the parity checker and the per-stage parity file split.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M0-bootstrap. go.mod (module github.com/megascan/gpui-go, go 1.27, keep the installed requires, internal/deps blank imports), LICENSE, NOTICE, AGENT.md, TECH_DEBT.md, .gitignore (/_ext), doc.go, and ci.yml with the ubuntu / macos-14 / windows-latest matrix, written once so no later stage edits it.

pieces.name: paritycheck
pieces.task: Matrix validator CLI (no upstream rescan) with flags -area, -done, -all-done, -allow-owner, -lint; exact checks and status vocabulary are in the STAGES.md section. Unit tests with fixture tables.

pieces.name: parity-split
pieces.task: Split linux.md, wgpu.md and core-examples.md by upstream-file heading as the 'Parity file split' table in STAGES.md says; update PARITY.md sections 2 and 8; totals stay 6706 items and 869 tests.

stages.name: M0-foundation
stages.goal: Port gpui_util, refineable and collections, add Option[T], and write the refinegen generator.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M0-foundation. gpuiutil (gpui_util lib.rs plus the Option[T] value type), refineable (Refineable, Cascade), refinegen for the //gpui:refineable directive emitting <file>_gen.go with Option fields, golden test. gpui_tokio rows are n/a:D-TOKIO.

pieces.name: collections
pieces.task: collections.rs and vecmap.rs (VecMap with entry API, hash aliases) and the 19 tests of vecmap_tests.rs as TestVecmap_*.

stages.name: M0-scheduler-core
stages.goal: Port the scheduler crate's clock, scheduler contract and executors with coroutine tasks.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M0-scheduler-core. clock.go, scheduler.go, executor.go per DESIGN 5.6 and 6.3: Scheduler interface, Runnable, Timer, executors, Task[T] as an iter.Pull coroutine (Await, Cancel, Detach), Oneshot, Chan, Select, Join, Yield. No goroutine leaks on cancel.

stages.name: M0-scheduler-test
stages.goal: Port the deterministic TestScheduler and all 31 scheduler tests.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M0-scheduler-test. test_scheduler.rs (seeded candidate selection with priority weights, parking, timeout ticks, virtual clock, PCG rng) and the 31 tests of tests.rs; the same seed must give the same trace.

stages.name: M0-sumtree
stages.goal: Port the sum_tree crate with its 11 tests.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M0-sumtree. sum_tree.rs, cursor.rs, tree_map.rs, property_test.rs with Item / Summary / Dimension / SeekTarget as generic interfaces, iter.Seq iteration, identical node shapes; must not import gpui.

stages.name: M0-a11y-schema
stages.goal: Pure-Go copy of the AccessKit 0.24 data model that elements, windows and adapters share.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M0-a11y-schema. Package a11y from accesskit-0.24.1 lib.rs and geometry.rs: Role, Action and the other enums with identical numeric values, Node with every property accessor, Tree, TreeUpdate, ActionRequest, the three handler interfaces, geometry. Files directly in a11y/ only.

stages.name: M0-jsonschema
stages.goal: In-repo JSON Schema reflector used for action schemas (D-SCHEMA).
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M0-jsonschema. Generator, Reflect(reflect.Type), Schema marshalled with encoding/json/v2, covering what schemars emits for upstream action structs; table-driven tests.

stages.name: M0-etagere
stages.goal: Port etagere's BucketedAtlasAllocator for the three atlas back ends.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M0-etagere. etagere-0.2.15 bucketed.rs with AllocID, Allocation, AllocatorOptions and int32 geometry; same shelf and bucket selection and id encoding; all its unit tests.

stages.name: M0-lyon
stages.goal: Port the lyon_path / lyon_geom subset that gpui's PathBuilder uses.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M0-lyon. Only what gpui/src/path_builder.rs:3-9 imports: Path, Builder, WithSvg, events, ArcFlags, Polygon, enums, math types, bezier segments, SVG arc conversion; float32 maths in upstream order; tests of the ported functions.

stages.goal: Port the flexbox algorithm and pass every flex fixture.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M0-taffy-flexbox. compute/flexbox.rs (3460 LOC) with inline tests in upstream step order; replace the stub; enable the flex fixture category and pass all of it.

stages.goal: Port grid track sizing and alignment; the whole fixture suite passes.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M0-taffy-grid-sizing. compute/grid/mod.rs, track_sizing.rs, alignment.rs; replace computeGridLayout, delete the package stubs.go, enable every remaining category: all 6505 fixtures pass.

stages.name: M0-taffy-handwritten-tests
stages.goal: Port taffy's hand-written integration tests.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M0-taffy-handwritten-tests. _ext/taffy/tests/hand_written/*.rs (26 files) as hand_written_<name>_test.go, one Go test per upstream test; fix engine bugs they expose.

stages.name: M0-geometry
stages.goal: Port geometry, color and the string types of the root package.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M0-geometry. geometry.rs and color.rs in full with the two families of DESIGN 6.1 (numeric Point[T] etc. and PointOf[T] etc.), unit types, Length, refinegen output for Bounds / Edges / Corners, SharedString, Option alias. No taffy conversions here.

stages.name: M0-contracts
stages.goal: Land the compiling skeleton of every cross-stage root contract so other lanes can build against it.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M0-contracts. gpui.go (gpui.rs) plus stubs.go declaring DESIGN 6.2-6.6, 6.10, 6.11 with exact names and signatures and panicking bodies; docs/api-contracts.md (stub protocol, mixin binding, handle rules); contracts_test.go compiles the DESIGN usage snippets.

stages.name: M0-platform-types
stages.goal: Port platform.rs: every platform interface and platform data type.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M0-platform-types. platform.rs (4116 LOC, 22 tests) and the small platform/* files: Platform, PlatformWindow and the other interfaces method for method, Defaults embeddables, all data types, image decode, atlas types, RawWindowHandle. js-incompatible decoders go in a !js file.

stages.name: M0-input-types
stages.goal: Port keystrokes, input events, the input handler, actions and the small app-level helpers.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M0-input-types. platform/keystroke.rs, interactive.rs, input.rs, action.rs (registry, RegisterAction from init, json/v2 Build, schema), queue.rs, global.rs, seeds.rs, assets.rs, util.rs (real Fluent[S] mixin), colors.rs. Window-dependent gpui::tests become blocked:M0-blocked-tests.

pieces.name: actiongen
pieces.task: Generator for the //gpui:action directive (namespace, name, no_json, no_register, deprecated_aliases, deprecated) emitting <file>_gen.go with Name, BoxedClone, PartialEq and the init registration, mirroring derive_action.rs and register_action.rs; golden tests. Needs only DESIGN 6.4.

stages.name: M0-scene
stages.goal: Port the scene, its primitives, the bounds tree and path building.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M0-scene. scene.rs, bounds_tree.rs, path_builder.rs, path_winding.rs. Primitive structs keep upstream field order and 4-byte fields; scene_layout_test.go pins sizes and offsets against the WGSL, Metal and HLSL structs; Batches() as iter.Seq; PathBuilder on internal/lyon plus okage stroking.

stages.name: M0-text-core
stages.goal: Port the text system front end: fonts, line layout cache and line wrapping.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M0-text-core. text_system.rs, font_fallbacks.rs, font_features.rs, line_layout.rs, line_wrapper.rs with go-text segmenter for line breaking; UTF-8 byte offsets; painting (line.rs) comes later.

stages.name: M0-profiler-core
stages.goal: Port the task and action profiler that executors and dispatchers call.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M0-profiler-core. profiler.rs (15 tests), profiler/actions.rs, profiler/hang/monitor.rs; the cargo feature becomes build tag gpui_profiler with one symbol per cfg pair in profiler_on.go / profiler_off.go.

stages.name: M0-entities
stages.goal: Port the entity map, subscriptions, executors and the dispatchers behind them.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M0-entities. app/entity_map.rs (handles per DESIGN 5.2, leases, weak handles, leak detector), subscription.rs, executor.rs, platform_scheduler.rs, threaded_dispatcher.rs, test dispatcher; 29 tests.

stages.name: M0-app
stages.goal: Port app.rs: App, Application and the effect system.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M0-app. app.rs (4031 LOC): Application, App fields, entity create / update / read, the Effect flush loop and its ordering, observers, globals, window map with leases, quit handling, keystroke observers, drags, displays, HTTPClient, AppContext primitives. Keymap, window and text calls go through stubs.

stages.name: M0-app-contexts
stages.goal: Port Context[T], the async contexts, the asset cache, the test macro runtime and TestPlatform.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M0-app-contexts. app/context.rs, app/async_context.rs, asset_cache.rs, testing.go (RunTest with seeds / iterations / retries, PropertyTest), platform/test platform, window and display method for method.

stages.name: M0-test-contexts
stages.goal: Port TestAppContext, TestApp, HeadlessAppContext and VisualTestContext; first gpui::tests run.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M0-test-contexts. app/test_context.rs, test_app.rs, headless_app_context.rs, visual_test_context.rs with the end-of-run leak report; port every earlier gpui::test that needs no window; window ones stay blocked:M0-blocked-tests.

stages.name: M0-keymap
stages.goal: Port the keymap, key contexts, the key dispatch tree and tab stops.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M0-keymap. keymap.rs (24 tests), keymap/binding.rs, keymap/context.rs (11), key_dispatch.rs (5 plain tests now, 20 gpui::tests blocked:M0-blocked-tests), tab_stop.rs (10).

stages.name: M0-gestures-spring
stages.goal: Port touch gesture recognition and spring animation maths.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M0-gestures-spring. gestures.rs (37 tests) and spring.rs (11 tests): pure state machines and float maths, time through scheduler.Instant.

stages.name: M0-style
stages.goal: Port Style, the Styled mixin and the generator for its 3099 macro methods.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M0-style. style.rs (fields in upstream order, refinements via refinegen), styled.rs (Styled[S] with 116 hand-written methods), stylegen porting gpui_macros/src/styles.rs to emit styled_gen.go; a test compares the method set with styled-methods.tsv.

stages.name: M0-element
stages.goal: Port the element machinery, views, the taffy bridge and inspector ids.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M0-element. element.rs (Element[RL, PP], typed drawable with phase panics, AnyElement, Component, Parent[S]), view.rs, taffy.rs (TaffyLayoutEngine and every gpui-to-taffy conversion with device-pixel rounding), inspector.rs.

stages.name: M0-window-core
stages.goal: Port the first third of window.rs: window types, focus handles, frames and Window construction.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M0-window-core. window.rs:1-2561 and 7891-8411 into window.go: invalidator, focus handles, hitbox and tooltip types, Frame, Window struct, pending input state, Window::new with platform callbacks, ContentMask, window handles, ElementID, PaintQuad.

stages.name: M0-window-paint
stages.goal: Port the middle of window.rs: state accessors, the draw cycle, element state and painting.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M0-window-paint. window.rs:2562-5700 into window_paint.go: focus and state accessors, observers, draw and draw_roots, tooltips, deferred draws, reuse ranges, content mask / offset / opacity, with_element_state, every paint_* method; upstream's order of operations.

stages.name: M0-window-dispatch
stages.goal: Port the last third of window.rs: layout requests, hitboxes, event and key dispatch, prompts.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M0-window-dispatch. window.rs:5700-7890 into window_dispatch.go and window/prompts.rs: layout, hitboxes, listeners, dispatch_event, touch, mouse, key dispatch with pending input, action dispatch, bindings queries. Add the smoke test with a hand-written Element.

stages.name: M0-div-api
stages.goal: Port the builder half of div.rs: Interactivity and the interactive mixins.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M0-div-api. div.rs:1-1904 plus the Interactivity struct: Interactive[S] and StatefulInteractive[S] mixin methods, listener types, NewDiv, the Div struct with its four mixins bound in the constructor.

stages.name: M0-div-paint
stages.goal: Port the layout, prepaint and paint half of div.rs with its tests.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M0-div-paint. div.rs:1905-4539: Element impl for Div, Interactivity layout / prepaint / paint, tooltip machinery, Stateful[E], ScrollHandle; the 28 div tests and the element.rs gpui::test.

stages.name: M0-text-elements
stages.goal: Port shaped-line painting and the text elements.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M0-text-elements. text_system/line.rs (ShapedLine, WrappedLine, decoration painting; 12 tests) and elements/text.rs (string elements, StyledText, InteractiveText; 2 tests).

stages.name: M0-window-tests
stages.goal: Port the window.rs test modules and fix what they expose.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M0-window-tests. window.rs:8412-11169: the 47 tests of mod tests and mod inspector_tests through RunTest. First full run of draw and dispatch under upstream's tests: fix the window and div code, not the tests.

stages.name: M0-blocked-tests
stages.goal: Port every test that was waiting for windows and elements.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M0-blocked-tests. Port all rows with status blocked:M0-blocked-tests (key_dispatch 20, interactive 2, input 2, app, test_context 8, test_app 4, line_wrapper 1, others) and fix the code under test. No core row stays blocked on an M0 stage.

stages.name: M0-elements-basic
stages.goal: Port anchored, animation, canvas, container query, deferred, surface and uniform list.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M0-elements-basic. elements/anchored.rs, animation.rs, canvas.rs, container_query.rs, deferred.rs, surface.rs, uniform_list.rs with their 22 tests; each element embeds and binds the mixins upstream implements for it.

stages.name: M0-list
stages.goal: Port the variable-height list element and its 41 tests.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M0-list. elements/list.rs (3883 LOC): List, ListState over a sumtree, alignment, follow modes, measuring, scroll anchors, splice / reset, and the 41 gpui::tests.

stages.name: M0-elements-media
stages.goal: Port the image and SVG elements, the image cache and the SVG renderer.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M0-elements-media. elements/img.rs, image_cache.rs, svg.rs and svg_renderer.rs on xo/okage (19 tests). L-SVGTEXT and L-JPEG are the only allowed differences.

stages.name: M0-window-a11y
stages.goal: Port the window accessibility tree and native view hosting.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M0-window-a11y. window/a11y.rs (13 tests), window/a11y/debug.rs, window/native_view.rs (11 gpui::tests); replaces the a11y and native-view stubs left by the window stages.

stages.name: M0-exit
stages.goal: Close M0: audit the headless core, port the integration tests, open the PR and get CI green on three OSes.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M0-exit. Port gpui/tests and gpui_macros/tests; audit stubs.go leftovers, M0 parity rows, strict leak mode, race tests, cross-vet of root and leaf packages; fold debt files; commit finished M0 stages only, push, open the draft PR against dev, fix CI on macOS and Windows.

stages.name: M1-wayland-ffi
stages.goal: Build the Wayland binding: purego runtime over libwayland-client, the protocol generator, generated protocols and a window + GPU surface spike.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M1-wayland-ffi. Package wl (purego over libwayland-client and libwayland-cursor, proxies via wl_proxy_marshal_array_flags, one dispatcher callback, real wl_display / wl_surface pointers), wlgen from protocol XML to wlproto/*_gen.go for the listed protocols, and wlspike: xdg_toplevel plus wgpu surface clearing for N frames.

stages.name: M1-linux-ffi
stages.goal: purego bindings for xkbcommon and a minimal libxcb shim.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M1-linux-ffi. Package xkb over libxkbcommon and libxkbcommon-x11: Context, Keymap, State, keysyms, compose, mirroring the xkbcommon-rs calls gpui_linux uses; explicit Close; keymap tests.

pieces.name: xcbshim
pieces.task: purego over libxcb.so.1 (connect, error check, setup / screen visual lookup, flush, disconnect) only to give the wgpu surface a real xcb_connection_t pointer; its test needs DISPLAY and GPUI_TEST_DISPLAY=1.

stages.name: M1-x11-proto
stages.goal: Fill the X11 protocol gaps of jezek/xgb and port the XIM client.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M1-x11-proto. Find which extensions gpui_linux's x11 code uses that jezek/xgb lacks (xinput 2.4, xkb, present, sync, ...) and implement those requests, replies and events in package xext with x11rb-protocol's layouts; byte-fixture tests.

pieces.name: xim
pieces.task: Port the client side of zed-xim 0.4.0 with xim-parser and xim-ctext, limited to what xim_handler.rs and client.rs use, behind a transport interface; frame encode / decode tests from byte fixtures.

stages.name: M1-wgpu-context
stages.goal: Define the renderer contract and port the wgpu context, atlas and shader loading.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M1-wgpu-context. render/render.go (Renderer interface of DESIGN 6.9); render/wgpu native files: wgpu_context.rs, wgpu_atlas.rs over internal/etagere, byte-identical embedded WGSL with sha256 test, compile test of all four shader variants. Only package with cgo; GPU tests skip without an adapter.

stages.name: M1-wgpu-renderer
stages.goal: Port WgpuRenderer and the headless renderer.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M1-wgpu-renderer. wgpu_renderer.rs (2900 LOC, 10 tests): surface from RawWindowHandle, pipelines, instance buffers from scene slices, paths, sprites with subpixel fallback, device-lost recovery, WgpuHeadlessRenderer; add a solid-quad pixel test.

stages.name: M1-linux-common
stages.goal: Port the shared Linux platform layer: client contract, event loop, headless backend, xkb helpers and the D-Bus services.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M1-linux-common. LinuxClient and LinuxCommon, dispatcher with a main-goroutine event loop in place of calloop, headless client and window, platform.rs helpers and tests, power, notifications, portal and Secret Service over godbus. D-Bus code takes its connection as a parameter; tests never touch the user's bus or keyring.

stages.name: M1-wayland-client
stages.goal: Port the Wayland client: globals, seats, input, IME, data devices and outputs.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M1-wayland-client. wayland/client.rs (3454 LOC, 10 tests), serial.rs, display.rs, cursor.rs, wayland.rs; window methods it calls go in a package-local stubs.go; compositor tests gated by GPUI_TEST_DISPLAY=1.

stages.name: M1-wayland-window
stages.goal: Port the Wayland window, layer shell, popups and clipboard.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M1-wayland-window. wayland/window.rs (2627 LOC, 6 tests), layer_shell.rs, popup.rs, clipboard.rs; renderer through wgpu.NewRenderer with a Wayland RawWindowHandle; a11y.go seam returning nil; remove the package stubs.go.

stages.name: M1-x11-client
stages.goal: Port the X11 client: connection, input devices, xkb, XIM and event translation.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M1-x11-client. x11/client.rs (3219 LOC, 11 tests) on jezek/xgb plus internal/xext, event.rs, display.rs, xim_handler.rs, x11.rs; window methods in a package-local stubs.go; X server tests gated by GPUI_TEST_DISPLAY=1.

stages.name: M1-x11-window
stages.goal: Port the X11 window and clipboard.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M1-x11-window. x11/window.rs (2098 LOC) with the wgpu surface through internal/xcbshim, x11/clipboard.rs (1287 LOC, x11-clipboard semantics), a11y.go seam; remove the package stubs.go.

stages.name: M1-linux-platform
stages.goal: Port LinuxPlatform, backend selection and the gpui_platform entry points.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M1-linux-platform. LinuxPlatform (Platform impl), linux.rs, display_connection.rs with the display-mode tests; package platform (LockOSThread in init, Application, Headless, CurrentPlatform). The darwin / ios / windows / js files return a not-ported error until M4 so CI builds everywhere.

stages.name: M3-profiler-hang
stages.goal: Port hang detection and the debug frame overlay.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M3-profiler-hang. profiler/hang.rs (21 tests) and debug_overlay.rs (6 tests); replace their stubs.

stages.name: M3-profiler-journal
stages.goal: Port the profiler journal.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M3-profiler-journal. profiler/journal.rs (3544 LOC, 27 tests): data model, ring buffers, records, serialisation byte-compatible with upstream where the file defines a layout.

stages.name: M3-bench-randomized
stages.goal: Port the bench runtime, BenchAppContext and the randomized element tree.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M3-bench-randomized. bench.rs plus gpui_macros bench.rs as RunBench (D-BENCH), app/bench_context.rs (6 tests), randomized_element_tree.rs (6 tests), benches/focus_cleanup.rs.

stages.name: M3-root-misc
stages.goal: Finish the root package: inspector reflection, screen-capture and visual-test types, docs, and remove stubs.go.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M3-root-misc. Reflection-based inspector_reflection.go with its test, screen-capture and visual-test types (missing back ends blocked:owner), n/a rows for arena and hot_reload, Go rewrites of the upstream docs under docs/ (run de-slop), delete stubs.go.

stages.name: M1-exit
stages.goal: Close M1: hello_world opens on Wayland and X11 with quads drawn by wgpu, checked by screenshot.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M1-exit. Port examples/hello_world, write internal/cmd/shoot (run, capture only that window with grim, terminate, clean up; -x11, -may-exit), screenshot on Wayland and XWayland and Read both images, fix what the first end-to-end run exposes, commit finished stages, push, check CI.

stages.name: M2-gotext-layout
stages.goal: Port the Linux text system's font database, metrics and line shaping onto go-text/typesetting.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M2-gotext-layout. Package gotext implementing gpui.PlatformTextSystem from cosmic_text_system.rs: NewTextSystem, NewTextSystemWithoutSystemFonts, font matching and fallback order, metrics, LayoutLine with cluster to UTF-8 index mapping; rasterisation returns an error until the next stage.

stages.name: M2-gotext-raster
stages.goal: Port glyph raster bounds and rasterisation, and the layout benchmark.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M2-gotext-raster. GlyphRasterBounds and RasterizeGlyph (monochrome, subpixel, colour emoji, subpixel variants) with upstream's buffer formats and rounding; L-GLYPH on pixel-exact rows; remaining tests of the 30 and the layout_line bench.

stages.name: M2-exit
stages.goal: Close M2: text, SVG and images render on screen through the atlas.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M2-exit. Wire gotext into the Linux platform, port examples/internal/support, text, svg_example and image_example, screenshot them and hello_world, Read every image, fix atlas / glyph / sprite issues wherever they are, commit, push, check CI.

stages.name: M3-a11y-consumer-tree
stages.goal: Port the AccessKit consumer tree state.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M3-a11y-consumer-tree. accesskit_consumer-0.38.0 lib.rs and tree.rs with all tree.rs tests; node methods it needs go in a package stubs.go; create ext-a11y-consumer.md.

stages.name: M3-a11y-consumer-node
stages.goal: Port the consumer node API, iterators and filters.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M3-a11y-consumer-node. node.rs, iterators.rs, filters.rs with their unit tests.

stages.name: M3-a11y-consumer-text
stages.goal: Port the consumer text model.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M3-a11y-consumer-text. text.rs (2836 LOC) with its tests; remove the package stubs.go; all rows done.

stages.name: M3-a11y-atspi-common
stages.goal: Port the platform-neutral AT-SPI adapter layer.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M3-a11y-atspi-common. accesskit_atspi_common-0.19.1 (node.rs, adapter.rs, simplified.rs and the small files) behind an AdapterCallback interface, no D-Bus; unit tests as upstream.

stages.name: M3-a11y-atspi-bus
stages.goal: Port the AT-SPI D-Bus adapter that Linux windows use.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M3-a11y-atspi-bus. accesskit_unix-0.22.1 on godbus: a11y bus discovery, exported AT-SPI interfaces, events, and the public Adapter (NewAdapter, UpdateIfActive, UpdateWindowFocusState, SetRootWindowBounds). Tests use a private dbus-daemon, never the user's a11y bus.

stages.name: M3-platform-benches
stages.goal: Port the gpui_platform benches.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M3-platform-benches. gpui_platform/benches/*.rs (27 bench tests) as external-package benchmarks on gpui.RunBench and the headless renderer; skip without a GPU adapter.

stages.name: M3-examples-a
stages.goal: Port and run the layout and basic painting examples (13 programs).
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M3-examples-a. One package main per upstream example, straight port with assets; build, run through internal/cmd/shoot, Read each PNG and compare with what upstream draws. Bugs outside examples/ go to the handoff file with a repro.

stages.name: M3-examples-b
stages.goal: Port and run the text, focus, input-device and painting examples (11 programs).
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M3-examples-b. Same procedure as M3-examples-a. The a11y example only needs to run here; its exported tree is checked in M3-exit.

stages.name: M3-examples-c
stages.goal: Port and run the window, system-integration and image examples (15 programs).
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M3-examples-c. Same procedure as M3-examples-a. Keep upstream's OS gates (layer_shell Wayland-only, native_view* macOS-only with upstream's message elsewhere); never send to the user's notification daemon.

stages.name: M3-examples-d
stages.goal: Port and run the examples that carry upstream tests: view_example, testing, input, animation.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M3-examples-d. Same procedure as M3-examples-a, plus the upstream tests as Go tests (view_example 4, testing 7, input 3, animation 1); view_example is five files.

stages.name: M3-exit
stages.goal: Close M3: every example runs on Linux, accessibility is wired, handoffs are fixed, M0-M3 parity is complete.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M3-exit. Wire a11y/atspi into the Wayland and X11 windows, check examples/a11y over a private a11y bus, work through every handoff file, confirm one checked screenshot per example, run Linux tests, cross-vets and parity for M0-M3, fold debt, commit finished M0-M3 stages, push, CI green.

stages.name: M4-apple-ffi
stages.goal: Lay the Apple FFI foundation on purego/objc and port the dispatcher, display link, process info and keychain.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M4-apple-ffi. internal/objc, internal/cf, internal/gcd helpers (darwin incl. ios, no cgo), then dispatcher.rs, display_link.rs, process_info.rs, gpui_apple.rs, keychain.rs (tests touch only their own items). Smoke tests per binding file; tests run only in CI.

stages.name: M4-apple-text
stages.goal: Port the CoreText text system.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M4-apple-text. text_system.rs (6 tests) and open_type.rs with internal/ct and internal/cg bindings: font matching, metrics, LayoutLine with UTF-16 to UTF-8 mapping, glyph rasterisation.

stages.name: M4-apple-metal-atlas
stages.goal: Bind Metal, port the Metal atlas and load the shaders.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M4-apple-metal-atlas. internal/mtl bindings, metal_atlas.rs (6 tests) over internal/etagere, shaders.metal embedded byte for byte and compiled at start with newLibraryWithSource; CI test compiles it and resolves every shader function.

stages.name: M4-apple-metal-renderer
stages.goal: Port the Metal renderer.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M4-apple-metal-renderer. metal_renderer.rs (1903 LOC, 3 tests): MetalRenderer satisfying render.Renderer, instance buffer pool, one draw path per batch, path intermediate texture, sprites, surfaces, presentation, headless render-to-image.

stages.name: M4-macos-input
stages.goal: Start the macOS platform: AppKit bindings, events, keyboard, displays and pasteboard.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M4-macos-input. internal/appkit wrappers, events.rs, keyboard.rs, display.rs, display_link.rs (4 tests), window_appearance.rs, pasteboard.rs (6 tests on a uniquely named pasteboard), gpui_macos.rs.

stages.name: M4-macos-platform
stages.goal: Port MacPlatform, system notifications and screen capture.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M4-macos-platform. platform.rs (1680 LOC): MacPlatform implementing gpui.Platform with app delegate, menus, panels, credentials via the apple keychain; system_notifications.rs, screen_capture.rs.

stages.name: M4-macos-window
stages.goal: Port the macOS window.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M4-macos-window. window.rs (4344 LOC): MacWindow implementing gpui.PlatformWindow, NSWindow / NSView subclasses via objc, NSTextInputClient IME, drag and drop, fullscreen and tabs, display-link frames, MetalRenderer lifecycle.

stages.name: M4-macos-native-views
stages.goal: Port native view hosting on macOS.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M4-macos-native-views. window/native_views.rs (1622 LOC, 6 tests); add a11y.go with a nil adapter seam; macos.md rows complete.

stages.name: M4-macos-a11y
stages.goal: Port the macOS accessibility adapter and wire it into the window.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M4-macos-a11y. Package a11y/macos from accesskit_macos-0.26.3 on a11y/consumer and the objc helpers; wire it in platform/macos/a11y.go where upstream uses accesskit_macos.

stages.name: M4-windows-com
stages.goal: Lay the Windows foundation: COM helpers, Win32 procs, dispatcher, displays, vsync and settings.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M4-windows-com. internal/com (vtable calls, GUIDs, HRESULT errors, Go-implemented COM objects), internal/win32 procs, then util.rs, wrapper.rs, dispatcher.rs, display.rs, vsync.rs (2 tests), system_settings.rs. Struct-size tests; tests run only in CI.

stages.name: M4-windows-directwrite
stages.goal: Port the DirectWrite text system.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M4-windows-directwrite. internal/dwrite bindings and direct_write.rs (2076 LOC, 4 tests): fonts, fallback, metrics, LayoutLine with UTF-16 mapping, glyph rasterisation incl. colour emoji.

stages.name: M4-windows-d3d-atlas
stages.goal: Bind Direct3D 11, DXGI and DirectComposition, port devices and the atlas, load the HLSL shaders.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M4-windows-d3d-atlas. internal/d3d bindings, directx_devices.rs, directx_atlas.rs over internal/etagere, shaders.hlsl and alpha_correction.hlsl embedded byte for byte and compiled at start with D3DCompile using build.rs's entry points.

stages.name: M4-windows-directx-renderer
stages.goal: Port the DirectX renderer.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M4-windows-directx-renderer. directx_renderer.rs (2083 LOC): DirectXRenderer satisfying render.Renderer, swap chain and composition, pipelines, MSAA path target, sprites, resize, device-lost recovery.

stages.name: M4-windows-input-shell
stages.goal: Port Windows event handling, keyboard, direct manipulation, clipboard, dialogs, jump lists and notifications.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M4-windows-input-shell. events.rs (1844 LOC), keyboard.rs, direct_manipulation.rs, clipboard.rs, dialog.rs (6 tests), destination_list.rs, system_notifications.rs; clipboard tests behind an env switch.

stages.name: M4-windows-window-platform
stages.goal: Port the Windows window and WindowsPlatform.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M4-windows-window-platform. window.rs (2 tests) and platform.rs (4 tests): PlatformWindow and Platform implementations, drop target as a Go COM object, credentials via the credential manager (tests use and delete a unique target), a11y.go seam.

stages.name: M4-windows-a11y
stages.goal: Port the UI Automation adapter and wire it into the window.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M4-windows-a11y. Package a11y/windows from accesskit_windows-0.34.0 (UIA providers as Go COM objects, text providers, WM_GETOBJECT, tests); wire it in platform/windows/a11y.go.

stages.name: M4-web-wgpu-js
stages.goal: Make render/wgpu work in the browser.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M4-web-wgpu-js. The _js.go side of render/wgpu: WebBackendPreference, PreparedWebGraphics, async adapter / device acquisition, canvas surface. WebGL fallback rows are blocked:owner. The Linux build and tests must stay identical.

stages.name: M4-web-platform
stages.goal: Port the web platform, window, display, dispatcher and HTTP client.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M4-web-platform. platform.rs, window.rs, display.rs, dispatcher.rs (single-threaded mode; multi-threaded rows blocked:owner), viewport.rs, keyboard.rs, logging.rs, gpui_web.rs, http_client.rs on syscall/js; js.Func values released explicitly.

stages.name: M4-web-input-text
stages.goal: Port web events, the IME mirror and the web text system; select the web platform.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M4-web-input-text. events.rs, ime_mirror.rs, text_system.rs (gotext without system fonts plus canvas text), canvas_text.rs, canvas_fallback.rs, glyph_cache.rs, run_replacements.rs (21 tests under node via go_js_wasm_exec); platform_js.go returns the web platform.

stages.name: M4-web-example
stages.goal: Port the hello_web example and its test drivers.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M4-web-example. gpui_web/examples/hello_web as Go files with index.html, gallery.js and the test_*.mjs drivers adapted to a Go wasm binary; build it and run the node drivers that need no WebGPU. Browser check goes to OWNER-CHECKS.md; do not launch a browser.

stages.name: M4-ios
stages.goal: Port the iOS platform and its example as far as GOOS=ios allows.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M4-ios. platform/ios on platform/apple: application.rs, display.rs, events.rs, platform.rs, text_input.rs, window.rs with their 12 tests, plus examples/ios_ios and the Xcode wrapper. What Go cannot do on iOS is recorded per row as blocked:owner.

stages.name: M4-ci-macos
stages.goal: Select the macOS platform, push, and make the macOS CI job pass.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M4-ci-macos. platform_darwin.go returns MacPlatform; commit the Apple packages (first push), then loop on the macos-14 job with gh run view --log-failed until vet, tests and example builds pass; wait in the background. List Mac-only owner checks in OWNER-CHECKS.md.

stages.name: M4-ci-windows
stages.goal: Select the Windows platform, push, and make the Windows CI job pass.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M4-ci-windows. platform_windows.go returns WindowsPlatform; commit the Windows packages (first push), loop on the windows-latest job as in M4-ci-macos; add the Windows owner checks to OWNER-CHECKS.md.

stages.name: M4-exit
stages.goal: Final audit: the definition of done holds or every gap is listed.
stages.core: Full brief: STAGES.md section M4-exit. Run the Final verify list; paritycheck -all-done -rescan -lint; list rows still blocked:owner under 'awaiting owner' in PARITY.md without inventing L- ids; update PARITY totals, TECH_DEBT.md, AGENT.md, README.md (de-slop), OWNER-CHECKS.md; commit, push, CI green on three runners.
